title: Best Food Storage Containers (Tupperware) UK
short: Plastic food storage containers compared on leakproof seals, stacking and staining, tested with real food and shake tests, from £8 sets to space-saving nesting boxes.
intro: A food container's real test is whether it stays sealed when it's shaken in a bag, not whether the lid claims to be airtight. This guide compares containers tested by Mumsnet writer Lucy Cotterill, who stored a range of foods in each one and scored design, versatility, cleaning, storage and value, plus shake tests and water leak tests to check every leakproof claim.

products.name: Brilliance Food Storage Containers
products.best_for: Anyone who wants leakproof containers for lunches as well as leftovers
products.key_spec: Tritan plastic, two-clip lids with rubber seal, steam-vent clips, dishwasher, freezer and microwave safe
products.summary: Mumsnet's clear winner, with lids Lucy found faultless: two clips, a lipped design and a substantial rubber seal made them airtight and leakproof even with liquid inside, so she carried casserole to the office in her bag. Steam vents in the clips stop microwave splatter and she saw no staining from tomato sauces, though they cost more than most sets.
pros: Built-in clip vents release steam in the microwave
No staining after tomato sauce use

products.name: PRUTA Food Storage Containers
products.best_for: Home leftovers and freezer storage on a tight budget
products.key_spec: 17-piece set, stackable, mixed sizes, dishwasher, freezer and microwave safe
products.summary: Mumsnet found 17 containers for about £8 works out at just under 50p per box, with clear plastic that makes contents easy to see and a good mix of sizes. They sealed well but aren't leakproof, so Lucy wouldn't use them as a lunch box, and they discoloured a little after sauce-based foods.
pros: Stackable to save space, good mix of sizes
See-through plastic, fairly easy to clean
cons: Not leakproof, so not suited to carrying in a bag
Not as high quality as pricier options

products.name: Six Piece Container Set
products.best_for: Households wanting several airtight sizes that nest away neatly
products.key_spec: Six BPA-free containers, four-lock lids, nesting design, dishwasher, freezer and microwave safe
products.summary: Mumsnet found the four-lock closing system genuinely leakproof: Lucy stored soup with no issues and the tubs passed her water leak test with flying colours. They nest neatly and are sturdy enough to stack when full, though the containers are shallow and the largest 5.5L tub is unlikely to get much use.
pros: Airtight and leakproof, passed a water leak test
Range of sizes in the set
Good value at the sale price
cons: The largest tub (5.5L) is too big for most uses

products.name: Nest Lock Containers
products.best_for: Small kitchens where cupboard space and lost lids are the problem
products.key_spec: Five nesting containers, colour-coded bases, lids that clip together, dishwasher, freezer and microwave safe
products.summary: Mumsnet found each container nests inside the next and the lids clip together in one pile, so cupboards stay tidy. Colour-coded dots on the bases make matching lids easy, and the set scored top marks for seal quality in Lucy's shake test, though it's expensive.
pros: Space-saving nesting design with stackable lids
Airtight and leakproof, top marks in the shake test

products.name: Snack Capsule To Go
products.best_for: Packing small wet and dry snacks separately
products.key_spec: 515ml capsule, lift-out compartment, removable spork, airtight and leakproof
products.summary: Mumsnet found the two sections ideal for keeping wet and dry foods apart, such as granola and yoghurt, and it didn't leak even with cereal and milk. It's fridge and freezer safe and microwaveable with the lid off, but only suits small snacks and younger children may struggle with the twist-to-open lid.
cons: Colour can't be chosen on Amazon
Younger children may struggle to twist it open

products.name: Two Compartment Containers
products.best_for: Portioning batch-cooked meals for the fridge and freezer
products.key_spec: Ten containers, two compartments, domed lids, nesting design
products.summary: Mumsnet found these easy to stack in a fridge or freezer after a big batch cook, letting Lucy portion out whole meals to reheat in the microwave. At £14 for ten they're great value for beginners, but the plastic is thin and might crack over time, and they're leak-resistant rather than leakproof.
pros: Ideal for meal planning and portion control
cons: Thin plastic that may crack over time
Not leakproof, so not for carrying in a bag
Won't last as long as sturdier designs

guide.q: Do my containers need to be leakproof?
guide.a: Only if they're going in a bag. If you're taking sauce-based lunches to work or school you need something properly leakproof, like the Sistema Brilliance or LocknLock here, which passed shake and water leak tests. For fridge, freezer and cupboard storage at home, a cheaper set such as the IKEA PRUTA is fine.

Mumsnet notes most containers are BPA-free plastic because it's durable and practical, and that even the best glass containers are heavy and prone to shattering if dropped, so plastic suits families better. Bamboo and silicone are further options.

guide.q: How do I stop containers staining?
guide.a: Highly pigmented sauces such as bolognese and chilli are the usual cause. In testing the Sistema Brilliance showed no staining even after tomato sauce, while the IKEA PRUTA discoloured a little. Look for rounded corners that won't trap food, and check reviews for staining before buying.

guide.q: How many containers do I need?
guide.a: It depends on your household size, how much you batch cook, how often you have leftovers and whether you pack lunches. Mumsnet suggests an assortment of sizes works best for most families, using some for leftovers, some for snacks and some for freezer meals, and choosing nesting or stackable designs to save cupboard space.
